scope.summary: Native and embedded focus/accessibility models support keyboard-only and screen-reader completion.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard-only and screen-reader users complete every P0 native-shell and embedded-content journey with coherent focus, names, roles, values, state, and transition announcements.
[positive] Run the P0 journey corpus with keyboard and Narrator/UIA, proving deterministic focus order and actionable announcements across native/embedded boundaries.
[negative] Hidden, unloaded, disabled, or offscreen controls are not exposed as actionable, and focus cannot disappear into an unobservable embedded surface.
[failure_recovery] Renderer loss or navigation rebuild restores focus to a stable Stage control and announces the failure and available recovery action.
[concurrency] Parallel model or background actions cannot steal keyboard/screen-reader focus; every focus mutation remains attributable to its window and action.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
Legacy Stage code (WP-12) must not silently constrain this MT (STAGE-DEC-017).
Do not duplicate ArtifactStore, WP-1 ToolGate/process/promotion, or Loom authority.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

planning_metadata.implementation_note: Planning-stage MT. Exact owned_files, code anchors, and proof_commands are bound at the L00 integration baseline. Deep spec detail lives in corpus_refs; acceptance_criteria carry the provable closure unit and the positive/negative/failure_recovery/concurrency case groups.
